toolResult.reason: Wrote design.md (Context/Goals/Decisions D1-D7/Risks/Open Questions/Migration), spec.md (4 Layer-1 requirements with scenarios covering all acceptance criteria), and tasks.md (T-01..T-06) under specrunner/changes/evidence-base/. Traced the real flow (oids.ts, gate.ts, achieved-assurance.ts, runtime local/managed adapters, workspace materializer bootstrap commit, adopt-commits/resume) before designing. Core: job base = first parent of synthesizedCommits[0] (no new state field), generic runTestsOnSynthesizedTree port method for red, HEAD candidate for green (includes adopt-commits), removal of contamination detection + gate 3.5 + archive-floor P2.5 with base-red rebuilt on the Evidence Base. Full test enumeration incl. the widened archive-floor surface. No source edits — planning only.

findings.title: Req 4 deferral list missing captureHeadSha→null path
findings.rationale: Spec Requirement 4 enumerates deferral conditions ('non-forward type / unset scopedTestCommand / unavailable runtime / absent base/job-base reference / empty selection') but omits the new path introduced in this change: captureHeadSha returning null → strategy-deferred. Design D4 and Tasks T-03 specify this behavior, but the spec is incomplete as a standalone normative document.

findings.title: TC-014 implementation mechanism not specified
findings.rationale: TC-014 ('detectBaseImplementationContamination removed with no remaining importers') is categorized as a 'unit' test but the assertion is structural/static (compile-time property). T-06 typecheck green already catches this as a TypeScript compilation error. The test-cases.md does not clarify whether a separate runtime test is needed, risking a redundant grep-based test being added.

findings.title: Archive floor fail-closed (absent Evidence Base ref) has no spec scenario
findings.rationale: Requirement 3 scenario covers only the positive re-run case. The archive floor's fail-closed behavior when synthesizedCommits is empty/absent is specified in design D1 and covered by TC-018, but there is no corresponding normative spec scenario. TC-018 is sourced from tasks/design rather than spec, leaving a minor normative gap.

observations.title: D1 basis verified in both worktree and no-worktree paths
observations.rationale: Both workspace-materializer.ts (L226-242, worktree path) and local.ts (L429-443, no-worktree path) call appendSynthesizedCommit immediately after the bootstrap commit. The adopt-commits path appends only to the ledger tail. Design D1 claim 'synthesizedCommits[0] is stable across resume/re-run' is structurally correct.

observations.title: captureHeadSha already on port — no new port method needed for candidate resolution
observations.rationale: captureHeadSha(cwd) exists at L329 of RuntimeStrategy. Design D4 correctly uses this existing method for the green candidate, keeping the port extension minimal (only runTestsOnSynthesizedTree is net-new).

findings.title: BiteEvidenceRecord.baseOid JSDoc stale — describes test-materialize OID, now stores Evidence Base revision expression
findings.rationale: The comment says 'commit OID of the test-materialize step (base boundary)' but gate.ts:289 now stores evidenceBaseRev (a git revision expression like 'bootstrapSha^', not a 40-char OID) in this field. No behavioral impact since the archive floor re-derives the EB ref from resolveEvidenceBaseRev(state) rather than reading this field. However, state.json consumers or future maintainers may incorrectly treat this field as a real OID.

findings.title: Catch block diagnostic message 'runTestsAtCommit threw' is stale — try block now also covers runTestsOnSynthesizedTree
findings.rationale: The catch wrapping both runTestsOnSynthesizedTree (e) and runTestsAtCommit (f) still says 'biteEvidence: runTestsAtCommit threw: ...' from before the Evidence Base refactoring. Both methods are contractually never-throw, making this path practically unreachable, but if reached the message incorrectly attributes the throw to runTestsAtCommit.

findings.title: runTestsOnSynthesizedTree empty-overlay early return bypasses scopedTestCommand guard
findings.rationale: When overlayFiles.length === 0, the method returns { kind: 'ran', results: [] } before the scopedTestCommand check at line 1200. The port contract says 'MUST NOT run without a resolved scopedTestCommand — absent scopedTestCommand → unavailable'. Operationally harmless because gate (step 6 empty-selection defer) and archive floor (materializedTestFiles length guard) both short-circuit before passing an empty list to this method. But it is a technical contract violation.

observations.title: Existing e2e test uses testMaterializeOid as synthesizedCommits[0] — valid approximation of bootstrap semantics
observations.rationale: The test uses baseOid (test-materialize commit) as synthesizedCommits[0] so that [0]^ = the init commit (no impl). This differs from the real bootstrap commit pattern (request.md commit) but correctly tests the mechanism. evidence-base-e2e.test.ts uses a proper bootstrap commit structure for TC-001.

observations.title: TC-002 (first-run vs resume same EB tree) covered by unit test only — E2E integration for this property not added
observations.rationale: Design D7 mentioned adding TC-002 to bite-evidence-e2e-gate.test.ts as well, but only the unit test in evidence-base-oids.test.ts verifies it. Since resolveEvidenceBaseRev is a pure function, unit coverage is sufficient to pin the invariant. No gap in acceptance criteria.

findings.title: BiteEvidenceRecord.candidateOid JSDoc states 'implementer step OID' but now stores HEAD OID
findings.rationale: The JSDoc comment reads 'commit OID of the implementer step (candidate boundary)' but the gate now writes headOid (branch HEAD). No current code reads record.candidateOid to make decisions (archive floor re-derives all OIDs independently), so there is no runtime impact. However, future code that reads this field expecting the implementer commitOid would operate on a wrong assumption. The field semantics changed silently without updating the adjacent documentation.

findings.title: testDerivation dimension fails-closed when synthesizedCommits is absent — new coupling not pinned by test
findings.rationale: Previously, testDerivation (blob freeze + scenario freeze) was derivable for any job that had a test-materialize commitOid, regardless of synthesizedCommits. The new P2.5 check (evidenceBaseRev === null → early return) blocks BOTH biteEvidence AND testDerivation, even though testDerivation has no logical dependency on the Evidence Base. TC-005 pins biteEvidence fail-close for absent synthesizedCommits, but no test pins the case where floor constrains only testDerivation and synthesizedCommits is absent. The design diagnostic message ('biteEvidence/testDerivation: Evidence Base reference absent') explicitly names both dimensions as fail-closed, so the behavior is intentional — but is underpinned only for the biteEvidence dimension.

options.label: Accept as-is (design explicit, legacy jobs only, fail-closed is safe)
options.consequence: The testDerivation fail-closed coupling to evidenceBaseRev stays unverified by test. Only legacy pre-ledger jobs are affected; any job with a properly-run test-materialize will have synthesizedCommits.

options.label: Add a pinning test for testDerivation with absent synthesizedCommits
options.consequence: TC-005 gets a variant: floor: { testDerivation: 'frozen' } + synthesizedCommits: undefined → testDerivation absent. Minimal change, closes the coverage gap.

findings.title: runTestsOnSynthesizedTree tmp path lacks OID discriminator vs runTestsAtCommit
findings.rationale: The tmp path is 'specrunner-bite-evidence-synth-${Date.now()}'. The existing runTestsAtCommit uses 'specrunner-bite-evidence-${oid.slice(0,8)}-${Date.now()}' with an OID prefix. Under concurrent jobs on the same machine, two runTestsOnSynthesizedTree calls could collide on the same Date.now() value, causing git worktree add to fail and returning unavailable (fail-closed, no data corruption). Risk is low in practice but slightly higher than runTestsAtCommit due to the missing baseRev prefix.

observations.title: Managed runtime deferred at step 6 (unavailable), not step 5 (capability check) — design comment mismatch
observations.rationale: Design D6 comment says 'runtime capability missing → strategy-deferred' at step 5, but managed runtime has all methods defined (returning unavailable). For managed runtime, deferral occurs at step 6 (listCommitChangedFiles → unavailable) or step 8 (runTestsOnSynthesizedTree → unavailable), not at the capability check. Behavior is functionally correct (managed runtime is always deferred), but the comment overstates what step 5 catches.

observations.title: runTestsOnSynthesizedTree writes git show stdout as string — adequate for UTF-8 test files
observations.rationale: showResult.stdout is a string (SpawnResult.stdout: string), written via fs.writeFile(destPath, showResult.stdout). For TypeScript test files (UTF-8 text), this is correct. For binary or non-UTF-8 content, data could be silently corrupted. Test files are always text in this codebase. Pre-existing pattern shared with the git show usage in runTestsAtCommit.

observations.title: synthesizedCommits[0] = bootstrap commit invariant verified across all write paths
observations.rationale: appendSynthesizedCommit always appends to the end. buildInitialJobState does not initialize synthesizedCommits. workspace-materializer, local.ts, managed.ts each call appendSynthesizedCommit(state, bootstrapOid) as the first write after the bootstrap git commit, before any pipeline step runs. adopt-commits also appends to the end. The invariant that synthesizedCommits[0] is the bootstrap commit holds across all write paths.

findings.title: BiteEvidenceRecord.baseOid stores a revision expression, not a resolved OID
findings.rationale: gate.ts:289 sets `baseOid: evidenceBaseRev` where evidenceBaseRev is a git rev expression like 'abc1234^', not a resolved SHA. The field name *Oid conventionally means a resolved 40-char SHA throughout this codebase. No current production consumer resolves baseOid as a SHA (archive floor re-derives EB via resolveEvidenceBaseRev(state)), so there is no breakage, but the naming will mislead future readers. Fix: rename field to baseRef or evidenceBaseRef (optional field, backward-compatible transition).

findings.title: P2.5 EB ref check gates testDerivation even though testDerivation does not use the Evidence Base
findings.rationale: The shared precondition block at P2.5 returns early for both biteEvidence and testDerivation when synthesizedCommits is absent. testDerivation (blob freeze + scenario revision binding) is logically independent of the Evidence Base — it only needs baseOid and finalHeadOid. A floor with testDerivation:frozen but no biteEvidence, on a job without synthesizedCommits, would lose testDerivation assurance unnecessarily. The achieved-assurance.test.ts pins this behavior intentionally (fail-closed). Practical impact is low because modern jobs always have synthesizedCommits. Fix: guard P2.5 with if (floorConstrainsBite) so testDerivation skips the EB check.

observations.title: synthesizedCommits[0] is set to the test-materialize commit (simplified vs real bootstrap pattern)
observations.rationale: The makeState helper uses synthesizedCommits: [baseOid] where baseOid is the test-materialize commit, not a true bootstrap commit. It works because baseOid^ (test-case-gen commit) happens to be impl-absent. The evidence-base-e2e.test.ts has the semantically correct structure. This test remains a valid regression suite for the overall gate + floor path; no fix required.
